title: Private control plane: deploy sequence, scale ops, and KMS/cert rotation runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures a pragmatic end-to-end sequence for: initial private control plane deployment (VPC and on-prem flavors), routine scale operations, and cryptographic rotations (KMS/HSM + TLS certs). It bundles Terraform module notes and an upgrade/rollback plan. The intent is an actionable checklist for SREs and platform engineers; keep this file as the quick-step operational guide and link to deeper docs for protocol-level details.

Who should use this:
- Platform engineers performing initial installs or upgrades
- Solutions engineers running scaled demos / customer acceptance
- SREs responsible for run-time rotations and emergency rollback

Assumptions & conventions:
- "controlplane" refers to Redwood Private control-plane components (API server, admin UI, config-store, auditor, keystore proxies).
- Terraform root uses modules under modules/private_controlplane/ and modules/networking/. The canonical root repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-private-controlplane
- We use cloud- or customer-managed KMS. Module name: module.ri_kms (abstraction with providers: aws|gcp|onprem-hsm).
- DNS records are managed by module.ri_dns with delegated zone name (customer-owned).
- All commands expect a working `env` file with TF_VAR_* and AWS/GCP creds loaded. Replace placeholders in capitals.

Initial setup (high-level sequence):
1) Pre-flight
   - Confirm account/region/network access, firewall rules, and cabling for on-prem clusters.
   - Collect artifacts: customer-admin email, delegated DNS zone id, KMS key id or HSM slot, and TLS CA bundle if custom.
   - Verify quotas: IPs, VPC cores, load balancers.
   - Create a ticket in PDPLAT- with target maintenance window (if customer-managed).

2) Networking & DNS (apply first)\   - Apply network module to create VPC/subnets or map to customer subnets.
   - Example (hosted VPC):
     export TF_VAR_vpc_id=""
     export TF_VAR_subnets="subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb"
     terraform init modules/networking && terraform apply -var-file=env.tfvars modules/networking
   - For on-prem, run inventory and set `TF_VAR_onprem=true` and map NICs.
   - Create DNS delegation records for the controlplane subdomain (controlplane.CUSTOMER_ZONE).

3) KMS/HSM & Secrets\   - If using cloud KMS: configure module.ri_kms with key resource id and grant the service principal.
   - If on-prem HSM: ensure HSM network access and that module.ri_kms.hsm_connector endpoint is reachable.
   - Example terraform snippet to import existing key:
     module "ri_kms" {
       source = "../../modules/ri_kms"
       key_id = "${KMS_KEY_ID}"
       provider = "aws"
     }
   - Verify key permissions: AWS IAM or GCP IAM binding for the ctl-plane service account.

4) Bootstrap control plane (initial apply)\   - Run bootstrap module to provision control plane instances, LB, and persistent volumes.
   - Recommended: apply in a canary fashion with count=1 for stateful components, confirm healthy, then scale.
   - Commands: 
     cd ./terraform/root/private_controlplane
     terraform init
     terraform plan -var-file=env.tfvars -out=plan.tfout
     terraform apply plan.tfout
   - Post-apply smoke checks: 
     - curl -k https://CONTROLPLANE_ADMIN_ENDPOINT/healthz (expect 200)
     - Check controlplane logs for bootstrap errors (journalctl /var/log/ctl-plane.log)

5) Post-deploy verification\   - Ensure controlplane version matches expected (admin UI -> About or /version endpoint).
   - Confirm metrics ingestion: controlplane.mtls_present, disk_free_bytes, rpc_latency_p95 < SLO.
   - Create initial backup of etcd/config-store using backup module: module.ri_backup.create_snapshot

Terraform module notes & gotchas:
- modules/private_controlplane/main.tf expects a `controlplane_image_tag` variable. Do not leave as `latest` in production — pin by semantic tag.
- modules/ri_bootstrap contains the machine-init user-data. If you modify cloud-init there, rollout will recreate instances. Use `create_before_destroy = true` where possible.
- module.ri_kms supports `external_hsm` boolean. When true, it expects hsm_endpoint and hsm_cert_pem; validate connectivity with `openssl s_client`.
- Use `terraform state rm` carefully for ad-hoc instance replacement; prefer using `terraform taint` and apply to recreate cleanly.
- Provider versions: lock provider constraints in root `required_providers` to prevent surprise upgrades mid-apply.

Scaling operations (day-2):
- Vertical vs horizontal: most controlplane components scale horizontally via the `instance_count` variable; stateful stores (etcd-like) require quorum-aware operations.

Quick scale-up procedure:
1) Validate health & backups\   - Ensure snapshot taken in last 30 minutes.
   - Check that controlplane error rate < 0.5% over last 10m.
2) Increase `instance_count` for stateless components (api, ui, worker) in variables.tf and run terraform apply.
   - Example: terraform apply -var "api_instance_count=3"
3) For stateful stores (config-store): follow the module's documented sequential add: add node -> wait for full replication -> repeat.
   - Do not add more than one replica to quorum simultaneously.
4) Validate autoscaling (if enabled): ensure autoscaler metrics (cpu_utilization, queue_depth) map to expected scale decisions.

Scale-down & evacuation:
- Scale-down should be a controlled drain: set new desired count, drain traffic (LB weight 0), wait for active sessions to drain, then terraform apply.
- For on-prem, confirm storage handoff for local PVs before deletion.

KMS / HSM key rotation (routine)
- Goal: rotate the key material without losing access to encrypted secrets.
- We use a primary/secondary key strategy where module.ri_kms maintains `active_key_id` and `previous_key_id` and supports key rewrap flows.

Rotation steps (cloud KMS):
1) Create a new key version or new key depending on provider capabilities.
2) Update module input `new_key_id` and run `terraform apply -target=module.ri_kms` to register it as `previous` while promoting it to `active` after rewrap step.
3) Perform a rewrap job: run the rewrap utility (internal tool: tools/kms-rewrap) against all secrets in secret-store: `python tools/kms-rewrap --from-key=OLD_KEY --to-key=NEW_KEY --parallel=20`
4) Monitor rewrap errors and retry.
5) After successful rewrap and validation, schedule destruction or set rotation policy on OLD_KEY.

If on-prem HSM: test connector with `hsm-tool --ping hsm://HSM_ENDPOINT` and confirm slot keys. The rotation may require coordination with HSM operator and can be non-trivial (often offline signing).

TLS certificate rotation (controlplane TLS):
- Certificates managed via module.ri_cert_manager which can integrate with ACME or customer CA.
- Preferred approach: implement staged rollout with dual-serving certs (old+new) for a short window.
- Steps:
  1) Generate new cert on CA or request via ACME with alternate SAN for rolling hostnames.
  2) Upload to secret-store and update module variable `tls_cert_ref` to new secret id.
  3) Apply change to 1 replica, validate, then roll through rest.
  4) Monitor TLS handshake errors and client failures.

Upgrade plan (minor/patch vs major):
- Minor/patch (backwards compatible):
  1) Create maintenance window (30–60m)\ 2) Take snapshot of config-store and backup images\ 3) Start a canary on a single replica with new `controlplane_image_tag`\ 4) Run smoke tests (login, token minting, sample inference call to a downstream node)\ 5) If green, roll via `terraform apply` across remaining replicas with `max_unavailable=1`
- Major (potentially incompatible):
  1) Create an extended maintenance window and full runbook with rollback gates\ 2) Deploy compatibility shim or migration job to transform persisted configs\ 3) Run canary and full regression suite against canary\  4) If failure, initiate rollback to previous `controlplane_image_tag` using pinned artifact and restore config-store snapshot if migrations modified state

Rollback playbook (fast path):
- If controlplane becomes unresponsive after an upgrade:
  1) Set service LB traffic to fallback model (if configured) or route to Dedicated instance (hosted fallback).\  2) Revert image tag in Terraform to PREVIOUS_TAG and `terraform apply` with target components first (api/ui).\  3) If config migration occurred, restore last working snapshot: `module.ri_backup.restore(snapshot_id)`\  4) Communicate status to customer and escalate to on-call SRE.

Validation checklist (post-change):
- API health (200 on /healthz)
- Auth flows: issue new token and exercise SSO if configured\- Controlplane metrics: token issuance latency, request success rate, etc.\- ETL: check that observability pipeline is receiving logs/traces

Troubleshooting notes & commands:
- View controlplane logs (systemd): `sudo journalctl -u ri-controlplane -f --since "10m"`\- Tail docker/k8s pod logs: `kubectl -n ri get pods && kubectl -n ri logs pod/<pod> -c controlplane` (only for private deployments using k8s)
- Recreate an instance without losing state: `terraform taint module.controlplane.aws_instance.api[0] && terraform apply`
- For TLS issues: `openssl s_client -connect CONTROLPLANE_HOST:443 -servername CONTROLPLANE_HOST` and examine certificate chain.

Open questions / follow-ups (to convert into tracked issues):
- Improve modules/private_controlplane to support canary image rollouts natively (feature request).
- Add automated post-apply smoke job in the root Terraform that runs a small lambda to validate endpoints.
- Document provider-specific HSM rotation steps per vendor (Entrust, Thales, AWS CloudHSM).

Appendix A — quick variable map (examples)\- TF_VAR_controlplane_image_tag = "v1.18.2-ri.2025-02-17"\- TF_VAR_api_instance_count = "3"\- TF_VAR_config_store_replicas = "3"\- TF_VAR_kms_key_id = "projects/x/locations/y/keyRings/z/cryptoKeys/ri-key"

Appendix B — emergency contact list\- On-call SRE: +1-555-0102 (oncall-sre@redwood.com)\- Platform eng lead: Rashmi Iyer

Notes: This document is intentionally concise and operational. For deeper design rationale and module API specs, see the linked artifacts above. After first successful run, capture any deviation to the ticket and update this doc (change log).
